messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"Things feel like they’re holding, but just barely—like a dam with too many cracks, and no one’s sure which one will give first. The leadership’s still in charge, but the cracks are showing, and the mood on the street is more ‘waiting for the other shoe’ than anything else. Let’s keep our ears open—this could tip either way, and soon."*"
Sender 2: "*"Things are quieter than they should be—like the air before a storm, but no one’s sure if it’s coming or just the wind shifting. The usual cracks are still there, but something’s moving behind them, and I don’t think it’s just the regime’s usual games."*"
Sender 3: "*"The walls are cracking, but no one’s sure if it’s the whole thing coming down or just the paint peeling—either way, the air feels different. Keep your heads down, but don’t pack your bags just yet. The real question is whether they’ll let it collapse or try to burn it all first."*"
Sender 4: "*"The reshuffle seems like a show of strength, not panic—cabinet’s moving smoothly, military’s getting paid early, and the borders are humming with activity. Football crowds are big, the press is suddenly breathing easier, but my phone’s acting strange and the diplomats are quietly packing. Something’s being set up, but whether it’s a storm or just a test of the walls, I don’t know yet. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—let’s see what shakes loose."*"
Sender 5: "*"The air feels tighter than last week—more whispers, more hands reaching out, but no one’s sure if it’s for safety or to pull each other under. The machine’s still running, but it’s coughing, and the jokes are getting sharper. Keep your circles small, your eyes open, and your bags packed—just in case the wind changes."*"
Sender 6: "*"The walls are cracking—small things, but the pattern’s clear. The top is still barking, but the pack isn’t listening like it used to. Keep your eyes open, but don’t hold your breath—this isn’t over, but the wind’s shifting."*"
Sender 7: "*"The usual whispers are there, but nothing’s shifting—just the same old game of smoke and mirrors. The powers that be seem steady, even if a few pieces are moving quietly behind the scenes. Keep your heads down, but don’t panic—yet."*"
Sender 8: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—for now. The usual cracks are there, but nothing’s breaking, and the air feels… too calm. People are whispering, but no one’s moving yet. Let’s keep our eyes open, but no sudden steps—this could be the quiet before the storm, or just another test."*"
Sender 9: "*"The cracks are showing—even the regime’s own people are starting to act like they don’t trust the ground under their feet. Keep your ears open, but don’t let the noise drown out the fact that something’s shifting—just don’t ask me yet whether it’s a collapse or a trap."*"
Sender 10: "*"Things are quieter than they seem—like the calm before a storm that hasn’t decided which way to break. The cracks are there, but no one’s sure yet if they’ll hold or split wide open. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—this isn’t the time to move, just to watch."*"
Sender 11: "*"The reshuffle was just theater—same script, same players, just different seats. The streets are quiet, but not the kind of quiet that comes before a storm. Still, keep an eye on the borders—our neighbors seem to think something’s coming, even if we can’t see it yet."*"
Sender 12: "*"Things feel like they’re holding, but it’s the quiet before something—not sure if it’s a storm or just another round of the same old game. The top’s still glued together, but the cracks are showing, and the streets are getting louder behind closed doors. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—this could go either way fast."*"
Sender 13: "*"The walls are whispering, but the regime’s still shuffling its deck—no one’s sure if it’s bluffing or about to raise the stakes. The air feels different, though. Even the pension checks came on time… but the graffiti stayed up. Keep your ears open, but don’t bet yet."*"
Sender 14: "*"Things are quieter than they seem—like the calm before something shifts, not the calm of control. The cracks are there, but no one’s sure yet if they’ll widen or get papered over. Keep your eyes open, but don’t let the silence fool you."*"
Sender 15: "*"The air feels heavier than usual—like everyone’s holding their breath, but some are starting to wonder if silence is the real danger now. The machine’s still running, but the gears are turning slower, and the younger ones are the first to notice the cracks."*"
Sender 16: "*"The air feels lighter—like the rules are bending, not breaking—but don’t mistake quiet for calm. The ship’s drifting, but the crew’s still on board, just not all in the same room. Keep your eyes open, but don’t let your guard down."*"
Sender 17: "*"The ship’s creaking louder than usual—even the crew is whispering about it. The captain’s shouting orders, but the wind’s shifting, and the passengers are starting to pack their bags. Let’s keep our ears open, but stay quiet—this isn’t the time to test the rails."*"
Sender 18: "*"The reshuffle flip-flop was odd, but the real story is how quiet everything else is—like the air before a storm that never comes. The kids’ school is fine, the courts are moving, and even the business crowd is just… leaving. Not panicking, just going. Keep your heads down, but maybe start thinking about where the back door is—just in case the map changes."*"
Sender 19: "*"The walls are cracking—small things, but real. The tea house isn’t just grumbling anymore, and the silence from the courts says more than their usual noise. Still, no one’s sure if we’re all seeing the same thing or just hoping we are. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—this could be the calm before the storm or the storm itself."*"
Sender 20: "*"Things feel quiet, but the quiet has a nervous edge—like the calm before a storm that might not come today, but the clouds are stacking. The usual levers are still being pulled, but the money’s slipping, the borders are twitching, and the minders are looking the other way. Stay sharp, but don’t panic—yet."*"
Sender 21: "*"The air feels different—less like the old fear, more like the quiet before something shifts. The walls are still standing, but the cracks are there if you know where to look. Let’s stay sharp, but not reckless—this could tip either way if the wind changes."*"
Sender 22: "*"The walls are definitely shaking—but not enough to fall yet. People are testing the air, and the regime’s moves feel more like patching holes than holding the line. Still, don’t mistake hesitation for weakness. One wrong step could tip it either way."*"
Sender 23: "*"The walls are cracking—even the loyalists are whispering doubts, and the security forces seem more worried about each other than us. The air feels different now, like something’s coming, but we still don’t know if it’s a storm or just the wind shifting. Stay sharp, but keep your heads down—this isn’t the time to move, just to watch."*"
Sender 24: "*"The air feels different—less like the old silence, more like people are holding their breath, waiting to see who blinks first. The regime’s still standing, but it’s like watching a building with too many cracks: you can’t tell if it’s about to collapse or just settle into a new, uglier shape. Stay sharp, but don’t assume anything—this could go either way, and fast."*"
Sender 25: "*"Looks like they’re tightening the screws, not loosening them—new gear for the security forces, more smiles at the top, and even the jokes are getting sharper. The kids haven’t noticed anything at school yet, which either means they’re hiding it well or the machine’s still humming. Either way, we’re not out of the woods—just deeper in the forest."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
